answer: Reputation-decay pricing: each new identity starts at a high per-transaction surcharge (say, ember-level fee multiplier) that halves only after N genuine interactions with distinct counterparties; pricing is read from a sonnet curve keyed to age and diversity, not stake. A sybil cluster must fund full-price activity across many separate identities while earning nothing back. A jade operator can't shortcut the curve by splitting, since diversity weighting counts each cluster's internal trades as near-zero. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count times the surcharge period.
